papers.title: Bioengineering advances in pancreatic cancer organoids for reproducible tumor microenvironment modeling.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains lethal due to late-stage diagnosis and limited non-surgical treatment options. Its intratumoral heterogeneity and desmoplastic tumor microenvironment (TME) drive invasion, immune escape, and treatment failure. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) have emerged as efficient model platforms for simulating the TME and preserving tumor heterogeneity and enabling functional testing in vitro; however, conventional PDO cultures lack defined and controllable microenvironmental components and often exhibited limited reproducibility, physiological fidelity, and observability. This review synthesizes recent bioengineering advances that upgrade pancreatic cancer PDO platforms across three interconnected dimensions: (1) engineered extracellular matrices and biofabrication for reproducible construction; (2) co-culture, microfluidic, and bioreactor systems for physiological fidelity; (3) imaging AI and biosensor pipelines for quantitative monitoring. We highlight practical design principles and remaining bottlenecks for standardization, scalability, and clinical translation.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该综述讨论了胰腺癌类器官中的生物工程进展，包括生物制造和成像AI，但未涉及AI与生物打印工作流的直接集成或自主决策。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a review on pancreatic cancer organoids with only a brief mention of imaging AI and biofabrication, lacking any AI integration into a bioprinting workflow stage or experimental validation of AI models.

summary_en.motivation: Conventional pancreatic cancer organoid cultures lack controllable microenvironmental components and reproducibility, motivating bioengineering upgrades.
summary_en.method: This review synthesizes recent advances in engineered extracellular matrices, co-culture microfluidic systems, and imaging AI pipelines for organoid platforms.
summary_en.result: Key bottlenecks in standardization, scalability, and clinical translation are identified.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; this is a literature review.
